sentence: This project tries to find out how a receptor senses copper outside cells and sends signals inside them, using C. elegans.
This project studies how telomeres are protected and how loss of that protection contributes to telomere-related disorders.
This project studies how the microbiome recovers after antibiotics and how owning pets affects that recovery.
This project studies how adenovirus changes the location and job of cellular RNA-binding proteins during infection.
This project builds a device that continuously monitors the activity of cells during gene therapy drug production.
This project explores ways to treat hemophilia A with small molecule drugs based on each patient's mutation.
This project studies how trophoblast cell lineage develops and works, because defects in it can cause early pregnancy loss.
This project tries to find markers of harmful T-cells in the heart and the heart cells that recruit them during inflammation of the heart muscle.
This project studies how the inflammasome in neutrophil progenitor cells affects inflammation and atherosclerosis in mice and humans.
This project builds porous polymer surfaces for growing cells that make it easier to study them with light and electron microscopy.
This project combines several datasets from a fiber-feeding study to find metabolic pathways linking high-fiber intake with the control of food intake.
This project studies how genetic differences in aging marmosets relate to features of late-onset Alzheimer's disease.
This project maps RNA modifications in metabolic cells from humans with obesity and type 2 diabetes to learn what they do.
This project tests therapies for treatment-resistant small cell lung cancer using patient-derived xenograft models and looks for markers of response.
This project builds a tool that reads RNA directly and maps many RNA modifications at single-base resolution in one analysis.
This project studies how antisense repeat RNA is made and tests treatments that target it in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis and frontotemporal dementia.
This project tests how drugs that block Jumonji enzymes affect small cell lung cancer in genetic mouse models.
This project engineers short proteins for gene therapy and tests whether they restore hearing and balance in mice.
This project measures synapse density and function in people with mood disorders to find synaptic problems linked to suicide risk.
